subproblems.statement: For all P, n, with 𝒟_n(ℝ^P) = GeometricCurrentOn univ n and 𝒟^n(ℝ^P) = TestFormOn univ n: (a) if E ⊆ ℝ^P is closed and X ∈ 𝒟_n(ℝ^P) satisfies X(ω) = 0 for every ω ∈ 𝒟^n(ℝ^P) whose tsupport is disjoint from E, then spt X ⊆ E; (b) spt X is closed for every X ∈ 𝒟_n(ℝ^P); (c) spt(A − B) ⊆ spt A ∪ spt B for A, B ∈ 𝒟_n(ℝ^P); (d) spt 0 = ∅; (e) spt ∂A ⊆ spt A for A ∈ 𝒟_{n+1}(ℝ^P). (Exact type of the comparator-accepted DAG declaration cmcsd_support_calculus, reused verbatim.)
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ), (∀ (E : Set (Euclid P)) (X : GeometricCurrentOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) n), IsClosed E → (∀ ω : TestFormOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) n, Disjoint (tsupport (ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) n)) E → X ω = 0) → X.support ⊆ E) ∧ (∀ X : GeometricCurrentOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) n, IsClosed X.support) ∧ (∀ A B : GeometricCurrentOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) n, (A - B).support ⊆ A.support ∪ B.support) ∧ (0 : GeometricCurrentOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) n).support = ∅ ∧ (∀ A : GeometricCurrentOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) (n + 1), A.boundary.support ⊆ A.support)
subproblems.natural_proof:
This is the comparator-accepted declaration cmcsd_support_calculus, reused with its identical frozen type; for completeness, its proof is as follows.
0. For T ∈ 𝒟_n(ℝ^P) let Z_T (GeometricCurrentOn.zeroRegion) be the union of all open W with compact closure, closure W ⊆ univ, on which T vanishes (T(ω) = 0 whenever tsupport ω ⊆ W); by definition spt T = univ \ Z_T = Z_Tᶜ.
1. (b) Z_T is a union of open sets, hence open (GeometricCurrentOn.isOpen_zeroRegion), so spt T = Z_Tᶜ is closed.
2. (a) Let x ∉ E. As E is closed there is r > 0 with closedBall(x, r) ∩ E = ∅. W := ball(x, r) is open, its closure lies in the compact closedBall(x, r) (ℝ^P is proper), so closure W is compact. If tsupport ω ⊆ W then tsupport ω ⊆ closedBall(x, r) is disjoint from E, hence X(ω) = 0 by hypothesis. Thus X vanishes on W, x ∈ W ⊆ Z_X and x ∉ spt X. Hence spt X ⊆ E.
3. (c) Let x ∉ spt A ∪ spt B. Then x ∈ W_A and x ∈ W_B for members W_A, W_B of the families defining Z_A, Z_B. W := W_A ∩ W_B is open, contains x and closure W ⊆ closure W_A is compact. If tsupport ω ⊆ W then (A − B)(ω) = A(ω) − B(ω) = 0 − 0 = 0 (the difference of currents acts pointwise). So x ∈ Z_{A−B}, x ∉ spt(A − B).
4. (d) For every x, ball(x, 1) is open with compact closure and the zero current vanishes on it, so Z_0 = univ and spt 0 = ∅.
5. (e) Let x ∉ spt A: x ∈ W, W open with compact closure, A vanishing on W. If ω ∈ 𝒟^n with tsupport ω ⊆ W, then tsupport dω ⊆ tsupport ω ⊆ W (tsupport_exteriorDerivative_subset), so ∂A(ω) = A(dω) = 0. Hence ∂A vanishes on W, x ∈ Z_{∂A} and x ∉ spt ∂A.
proof_key_steps: spt T is the complement of the open zero region (closedness)
support criterion: points off a closed E have a relatively compact ball avoiding E on which X vanishes
difference, zero current and boundary: intersect vanishing neighbourhoods; tsupport dω ⊆ tsupport ω

subproblems.title: A coefficient-norm bounded linear functional on test forms is a current (reused accepted declaration)
subproblems.statement: For all P, n, every U ⊆ ℝ^P, every linear L : 𝒟^n(U) = TestFormOn U n → ℝ and A ∈ ℝ such that |L(ω)| ≤ c·A whenever c > 0 and covectorEuclideanNorm(ω(x)) ≤ c for all x, there is Y ∈ GeometricCurrentOn U n with Y(ω) = L(ω) for every ω ∈ 𝒟^n(U). (Exact type of the comparator-accepted DAG declaration cmc_fc_sc_current_of_coeff_bound, reused verbatim.)
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (U : Set (Euclid P)) (L : TestFormOn U n →ₗ[ℝ] ℝ) (A : ℝ), (∀ (ω : TestFormOn U n) (c : ℝ), 0 < c → (∀ x, covectorEuclideanNorm ((ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) n) x) ≤ c) → |L ω| ≤ c * A) → ∃ Y : GeometricCurrentOn U n, ∀ ω : TestFormOn U n, Y ω = L ω
subproblems.natural_proof:
This is the comparator-accepted declaration cmc_fc_sc_current_of_coeff_bound, reused with its identical frozen type; for completeness, its proof is as follows.
1. Norm comparison. For an n-covector α on ℝ^P and an increasing multi-index I, |α(e_{I_1}, …, e_{I_n})| ≤ ‖α‖·∏‖e_{I_i}‖ = ‖α‖ (operator norm, standard basis vectors have norm 1). The Euclidean coefficient norm is the square root of a sum of at most P^n such squares, so |α| ≤ κ‖α‖ with κ := sqrt(P^n).
2. Continuity. A GeometricCurrentOn needs only: L(ω_j) → 0 whenever TestFormOnConverges ω_j 0. In that case there is a compact K ⊆ U with tsupport ω_j ⊆ K for all j and iteratedFDeriv ℝ 0 ω_j → 0 uniformly on K; since ‖iteratedFDeriv ℝ 0 f x‖ = ‖f x‖ (norm_iteratedFDeriv_zero), for every ε > 0 there is j₀ with κ‖ω_j(x)‖ ≤ ε for j ≥ j₀ and x ∈ K, and ω_j(x) = 0 for x ∉ K. Hence |ω_j(x)| ≤ ε for all x and j ≥ j₀, and the hypothesis (with c = ε > 0) gives |L(ω_j)| ≤ ε·A ≤ ε·max(A, 0). As ε > 0 is arbitrary, L(ω_j) → 0.
3. Put Y := ⟨L, step 2⟩ (structure GeometricCurrentOn with toCurrent := L). Then Y(ω) = L(ω) for every ω.
proof_key_steps: coefficient norm ≤ κ · operator norm
test-form convergence to 0 forces uniform convergence of the forms to 0, hence L(ω_j) → 0
package L with this continuity as a GeometricCurrentOn

subproblems.natural_proof:
Here U = univ; M_W(T) = sup{ofReal(T ω) : ω ∈ 𝒟^k, tsupport ω ⊆ W, |ω(x)| ≤ 1 ∀x} (massOn), M(T) = M_univ(T), and spt T = univ \ Z_T with Z_T = T.zeroRegion open.
1. (A0). Let X, ψ, c be as in (A0).
1.1. Apply (REP) with P = N, n = k, U = univ, T = X: univ is open, and for every open W (in particular W ⊂⊂ univ) M_W(X) ≤ M_univ(X) = M(X) < ∞ by GeometricCurrentOn.massOn_mono. We get μ and ξ with μ(K) < ∞ for compact K, M_W(X) = μ(W) for open W, ξ μ-a.e. strongly measurable, |ξ(x)(α)| ≤ |α| for all x, α, and X(ω) = ∫ ξ(x)(ω(x)) dμ for all ω ∈ 𝒟^k.
1.2. univ is open, so μ(univ) = M_univ(X) = M(X) < ∞: μ is a finite measure (IsFiniteMeasure).
1.3. Let Z := (spt X)ᶜ. Since spt X = univ \ Z_X, Z = Z_X is open (GeometricCurrentOn.isOpen_zeroRegion), so μ(Z) = M_Z(X). Every ω admissible for M_Z(X) has tsupport ω ⊆ Z, i.e. tsupport ω disjoint from spt X, so X(ω) = 0 by (VO) and ofReal(X ω) = 0; hence M_Z(X) = 0 (a supremum of a subset of {0}), μ(Z) = 0, and μ-a.e. x lies in spt X.
1.4. Therefore for μ-a.e. x: |ξ(x)(ψ(x))| ≤ |ψ(x)| ≤ c. By MeasureTheory.norm_integral_le_of_norm_le_const (finite μ, a.e. bound), |X(ψ)| = |∫ ξ(x)(ψ(x)) dμ| ≤ c·μ(univ).toReal = c·M(X).toReal.
2. (MB). M(T) is the supremum of ofReal(T ω) over ω with |ω(x)| ≤ 1 for all x. For such ω the hypothesis with c = 1 gives T ω ≤ |T ω| ≤ C·1, so ofReal(T ω) ≤ ofReal C; by sSup_le, M(T) ≤ ofReal C.
3. (LOC). η − η' ∈ 𝒟^k(ℝ^N) vanishes on W, so its support lies in the closed set Wᶜ and tsupport(η − η') ⊆ Wᶜ, which is disjoint from spt X ⊆ W. By (VO), X(η − η') = 0; by linearity X(η) − X(η') = X(η − η') = 0.
4. Mass of a difference. For A, B ∈ 𝒟_k(ℝ^N) and any W, M_W(A − B) ≤ M_W(A) + M_W(B): for admissible ω, −ω is admissible (tsupport(−ω) = tsupport ω, |−α| = |α| by covectorEuclideanNorm_neg), (A − B)(ω) = A(ω) − B(ω) = A(ω) + B(−ω), and ofReal(A ω + B(−ω)) ≤ ofReal(A ω) + ofReal(B(−ω)) ≤ M_W(A) + M_W(B) (ENNReal.ofReal_add_le, GeometricCurrentOn.le_massOn); take the supremum. Also, for A, B of degree k'+1, ∂(A − B) = ∂A − ∂B, since both sides evaluate at ω to A(dω) − B(dω) (GeometricCurrentOn.ext).
5. (NCD). Let X, Y be NC. By the reused support_calculus (c), spt(X − Y) ⊆ spt X ∪ spt Y; by (b), spt(X − Y) is closed, hence compact as a closed subset of the compact set spt X ∪ spt Y. By step 4 (W = univ), M(X − Y) ≤ M(X) + M(Y) < ∞. If k = 0, boundaryMassOn (X − Y) univ = 0 < ∞ by definition. If k = k'+1, boundaryMassOn (X − Y) univ = M(∂(X − Y)) = M(∂X − ∂Y) ≤ M(∂X) + M(∂Y) = boundaryMassOn X univ + boundaryMassOn Y univ < ∞ by step 4.
6. (NCB). Let X ∈ 𝒟_{k+1} with compact support and M(∂X) < ∞. By support_calculus (e), spt ∂X ⊆ spt X; by (b) spt ∂X is closed, hence compact. If k = 0, boundaryMassOn ∂X univ = 0 < ∞. If k = k'+1, boundaryMassOn ∂X univ = M(∂∂X) = M(0) (GeometricCurrentOn.boundary_boundary) and M(0) = 0 because every admissible ω gives ofReal(0(ω)) = ofReal 0 = 0; so it is < ∞.

subproblems.title: Cut-off smooth pull-back test forms agreeing with F^#ω and F^#dω near a compact set
subproblems.statement: For all N, N', k, every C^∞ map F : ℝ^N → ℝ^{N'} (ContDiff ℝ (⊤ : ℕ∞) F), every ω ∈ 𝒟^k(ℝ^{N'}) = TestFormOn univ k and every compact K ⊆ ℝ^N there are η ∈ 𝒟^k(ℝ^N) and an open W ⊇ K such that for all x ∈ W, η(x) = (ω(F x)).compContinuousLinearMap (fderiv ℝ F x) and exteriorDerivative η x = (exteriorDerivative ω (F x)).compContinuousLinearMap (fderiv ℝ F x).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (N N' k : ℕ) (F : Euclid N → Euclid N') (ω : TestFormOn (univ : Set (Euclid N')) k) (K : Set (Euclid N)), ContDiff ℝ (⊤ : ℕ∞) F → IsCompact K → ∃ (η : TestFormOn (univ : Set (Euclid N)) k) (W : Set (Euclid N)), IsOpen W ∧ K ⊆ W ∧ (∀ x ∈ W, (η : DifferentialForm (Euclid N) k) x = ((ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid N') k) (F x)).compContinuousLinearMap (fderiv ℝ F x)) ∧ ∀ x ∈ W, exteriorDerivative (η : DifferentialForm (Euclid N) k) x = (exteriorDerivative (ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid N') k) (F x)).compContinuousLinearMap (fderiv ℝ F x)
subproblems.natural_proof:
1. Smoothness of β(x) := (ω(F x)).compContinuousLinearMap (DF(x)). Let Φ := ContinuousAlternatingMap.compContinuousLinearMapCLM : (ℝ^N →L ℝ^{N'}) → (Covector ℝ^{N'} k →L Covector ℝ^N k), Φ(A)(α) = α.compContinuousLinearMap A. Φ is analytic on univ (ContinuousAlternatingMap.analyticOnNhd_compContinuousLinearMapCLM univ), hence C^∞. x ↦ DF(x) is C^∞ (contDiff_infty_iff_fderiv applied to the C^∞ map F) and x ↦ ω(F x) is C^∞ (ω is C^∞ as a test form, composed with F). Hence β = fun x => Φ(DF x)(ω(F x)) is C^∞ by ContDiff.clm_apply (the same argument proves the accepted lemma dpf_pb_smooth_pullback_isTestForm).
2. For every x, exteriorDerivative β x = (exteriorDerivative ω (F x)).compContinuousLinearMap (DF x): this is Mathlib's extDeriv_pullback (exteriorDerivative = extDeriv), applied with smoothness exponent ∞ ≥ minSmoothness ℝ 2, ω differentiable at F(x) and F C^∞ at x.
3. Cut-off function. O := thickening 1 K is open and contains K, and closure O ⊆ cthickening 1 K, which is compact because K is compact and ℝ^N is proper. By the smooth Urysohn lemma exists_contMDiffMap_one_nhds_of_subset_interior (ℝ^N is a Hausdorff, normal, σ-compact finite-dimensional manifold modelled on itself; K is closed and K ⊆ O = interior O) there is a C^∞ ζ : ℝ^N → [0,1] with ζ = 1 on a neighbourhood of K and ζ(x) = 0 for x ∉ O. (Equivalently: convolve the indicator of cthickening (1/2) K with a normalized ContDiffBump of radius 1/4.) Put W := interior {x : ζ x = 1}; W is open and K ⊆ W because {ζ = 1} ∈ 𝓝ˢ K. Since support ζ ⊆ O, tsupport ζ ⊆ closure O is compact.
4. Let η := fun x => ζ(x) • β(x). It is C^∞ (ContDiff.smul of the C^∞ scalar ζ and the C^∞ form β) and tsupport η ⊆ tsupport ζ is compact, so η is a test form with tsupport η ⊆ univ, i.e. η ∈ 𝒟^k(ℝ^N).
5. For x ∈ W, ζ(x) = 1, so η(x) = β(x) = (ω(F x)).compContinuousLinearMap (DF x).
6. For x ∈ W, η and β agree on the open neighbourhood W of x, so fderiv η x = fderiv β x (Filter.EventuallyEq.fderiv_eq) and therefore exteriorDerivative η x = alternatizeUncurryFin (fderiv η x) = alternatizeUncurryFin (fderiv β x) = exteriorDerivative β x = (exteriorDerivative ω (F x)).compContinuousLinearMap (DF x) by step 2.
proof_key_steps: F^#ω is C^∞: analytic precomposition operator, C^∞ derivative of F, ContDiff.clm_apply
d(F^#ω) = F^#(dω) everywhere by extDeriv_pullback
smooth cut-off ζ = 1 near K with compact support (smooth Urysohn on a thickening of K)
η := ζ·F^#ω is a test form equal to F^#ω on the open set W = interior{ζ = 1} ⊇ K
local equality on W gives equal derivatives, hence dη = F^#(dω) on W

subproblems.title: Smooth Λ-Lipschitz mollifications of a Λ-Lipschitz map
subproblems.statement: For all N, N', Λ ∈ ℝ≥0 and every Λ-Lipschitz F : ℝ^N → ℝ^{N'} there are maps Fs_j : ℝ^N → ℝ^{N'} (j ∈ ℕ), each C^∞ (ContDiff ℝ (⊤ : ℕ∞)) and Λ-Lipschitz, with dist(Fs_j(x), F(x)) ≤ Λ/(j+1) for all j and x.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (N N' : ℕ) (Λ : NNReal) (F : Euclid N → Euclid N'), LipschitzWith Λ F → ∃ Fs : ℕ → Euclid N → Euclid N', (∀ j, ContDiff ℝ (⊤ : ℕ∞) (Fs j)) ∧ (∀ j, LipschitzWith Λ (Fs j)) ∧ ∀ (j : ℕ) (x : Euclid N), dist (Fs j x) (F x) ≤ (Λ : ℝ) / ((j : ℝ) + 1)
subproblems.natural_proof:
1. Fix j and σ := 1/(j+1) > 0. Let φ : ContDiffBump (0 : ℝ^N) with rIn = σ/2 and rOut = σ, and ϕ := φ.normed volume. Then ϕ is C^∞, ϕ ≥ 0, ∫ ϕ = 1, support ϕ = ball(0, σ) and ϕ has compact support (ContDiffBump.contDiff_normed, nonneg_normed, integral_normed, support_normed_eq, hasCompactSupport_normed). Define Fs_j := ϕ ⋆[lsmul ℝ ℝ, volume] F, i.e. Fs_j(x) = ∫ ϕ(y) • F(x − y) dy.
2. Smoothness: F is continuous, hence locally integrable, and ϕ is C^∞ with compact support, so Fs_j is C^∞ by HasCompactSupport.contDiff_convolution_left.
3. Distance: for every x and y ∈ ball(x, σ), dist(F(y), F(x)) ≤ Λ·dist(y, x) ≤ Λσ. By ContDiffBump.dist_normed_convolution_le (F continuous, hence a.e. strongly measurable), dist(Fs_j(x), F(x)) ≤ Λσ = Λ/(j+1).
4. Lipschitz: for x, x' ∈ ℝ^N the integrands y ↦ ϕ(y)•F(x − y) and y ↦ ϕ(y)•F(x' − y) are continuous with compact support, hence integrable, and Fs_j(x) − Fs_j(x') = ∫ ϕ(y)•(F(x − y) − F(x' − y)) dy. Therefore ‖Fs_j(x) − Fs_j(x')‖ ≤ ∫ ϕ(y)·‖F(x − y) − F(x' − y)‖ dy ≤ ∫ ϕ(y)·Λ‖x − x'‖ dy = Λ‖x − x'‖, using ϕ ≥ 0, ∫ϕ = 1 (norm_integral_le_integral_norm, integral_mono). Hence Fs_j is Λ-Lipschitz (LipschitzWith.of_dist_le_mul).
5. The family (Fs_j) has all required properties.
proof_key_steps: normalized bump ϕ of radius 1/(j+1); Fs_j := ϕ ⋆ F
C^∞ by HasCompactSupport.contDiff_convolution_left
dist(Fs_j x, F x) ≤ Λ/(j+1) by ContDiffBump.dist_normed_convolution_le

subproblems.title: Affine homotopies ℝ^{N+1} → ℝ^{N'}: existence and derivative calculus at ι(t, x)
subproblems.statement: With ι(t,x) = WithLp.toLp 2 (Fin.cons t (WithLp.ofLp x)), e₀ = EuclideanSpace.single 0 1 and Jv = ι(0,v): (i) for all N, N' and C^∞ F, G : ℝ^N → ℝ^{N'} there is a C^∞ H : ℝ^{N+1} → ℝ^{N'} with H(ι(t,x)) = F(x) + t•(G(x) − F(x)) for all t ∈ ℝ, x ∈ ℝ^N; (ii) for all N, N', F, G : ℝ^N → ℝ^{N'}, H : ℝ^{N+1} → ℝ^{N'}, t ∈ ℝ, x ∈ ℝ^N, if F and G are differentiable at x, H is differentiable at ι(t,x) and H(ι(s,z)) = F(z) + s•(G(z) − F(z)) for all s, z, then DH(ι(t,x))e₀ = G(x) − F(x), DH(ι(t,x))(Jv) = DF(x)v + t•(DG(x)v − DF(x)v) for all v, and ‖DH(ι(t,x))‖ ≤ ‖G(x) − F(x)‖ + ‖DF(x) + t•(DG(x) − DF(x))‖.
subproblems.lean_statement: (∀ (N N' : ℕ) (F G : Euclid N → Euclid N'), ContDiff ℝ (⊤ : ℕ∞) F → ContDiff ℝ (⊤ : ℕ∞) G → ∃ H : Euclid (N + 1) → Euclid N', ContDiff ℝ (⊤ : ℕ∞) H ∧ ∀ (t : ℝ) (x : Euclid N), H (WithLp.toLp 2 (Fin.cons t (WithLp.ofLp x))) = F x + t • (G x - F x)) ∧ ∀ (N N' : ℕ) (F G : Euclid N → Euclid N') (H : Euclid (N + 1) → Euclid N') (t : ℝ) (x : Euclid N), DifferentiableAt ℝ F x → DifferentiableAt ℝ G x → DifferentiableAt ℝ H (WithLp.toLp 2 (Fin.cons t (WithLp.ofLp x))) → (∀ (s : ℝ) (z : Euclid N), H (WithLp.toLp 2 (Fin.cons s (WithLp.ofLp z))) = F z + s • (G z - F z)) → fderiv ℝ H (WithLp.toLp 2 (Fin.cons t (WithLp.ofLp x))) (EuclideanSpace.single 0 1) = G x - F x ∧ (∀ v : Euclid N, fderiv ℝ H (WithLp.toLp 2 (Fin.cons t (WithLp.ofLp x))) (WithLp.toLp 2 (Fin.cons 0 (WithLp.ofLp v))) = fderiv ℝ F x v + t • (fderiv ℝ G x v - fderiv ℝ F x v)) ∧ ‖fderiv ℝ H (WithLp.toLp 2 (Fin.cons t (WithLp.ofLp x)))‖ ≤ ‖G x - F x‖ + ‖fderiv ℝ F x + t • (fderiv ℝ G x - fderiv ℝ F x)‖
subproblems.natural_proof:
1. Coordinates. p₀(y) := (WithLp.ofLp y) 0 : ℝ^{N+1} → ℝ and tail(y) := WithLp.toLp 2 (Fin.tail (WithLp.ofLp y)) : ℝ^{N+1} → ℝ^N are continuous linear maps, and J(v) := WithLp.toLp 2 (Fin.cons 0 (WithLp.ofLp v)) is linear ℝ^N → ℝ^{N+1}, hence a continuous linear map (finite dimension). By Fin.cons_zero, Fin.tail_cons and Fin.cons_succ: p₀(ι(t,x)) = t, tail(ι(t,x)) = x, ι(s,z) = s•e₀ + J(z) (compare coordinates with Fin.cases), and every w ∈ ℝ^{N+1} satisfies w = p₀(w)•e₀ + J(tail w). Moreover ‖w‖² = p₀(w)² + ‖tail w‖² (EuclideanSpace.norm_eq, Fin.sum_univ_succ), so |p₀(w)| ≤ ‖w‖ and ‖tail w‖ ≤ ‖w‖.
2. (i) Define H(y) := F(tail y) + p₀(y)•(G(tail y) − F(tail y)). It is C^∞: compositions of C^∞ maps with continuous linear maps, a difference, a product of the C^∞ scalar p₀ with a C^∞ map, and a sum. By step 1, H(ι(t,x)) = F(x) + t•(G(x) − F(x)).
3. (ii) Let y₀ := ι(t,x) and D := fderiv ℝ H y₀, so H has derivative D at y₀.
3.1. The curve c(s) := ι(s,x) = s•e₀ + J(x) has derivative e₀ at every s. By the chain rule (HasFDerivAt.comp_hasDerivAt at s = t, c(t) = y₀), s ↦ H(c(s)) has derivative D(e₀) at t. But H(c(s)) = F(x) + s•(G(x) − F(x)) for all s, whose derivative is G(x) − F(x). By uniqueness of derivatives D(e₀) = G(x) − F(x).
3.2. The map ℓ(z) := ι(t,z) = t•e₀ + J(z) has derivative J at x, so z ↦ H(ℓ(z)) has derivative D ∘L J at x (chain rule, ℓ(x) = y₀). But H(ℓ(z)) = F(z) + t•(G(z) − F(z)) for all z, which has derivative DF(x) + t•(DG(x) − DF(x)) at x because F and G are differentiable at x. By uniqueness of Fréchet derivatives, D(Jv) = DF(x)v + t•(DG(x)v − DF(x)v) for all v.
3.3. Let A := DF(x) + t•(DG(x) − DF(x)). For w ∈ ℝ^{N+1}, steps 1, 3.1, 3.2 give D(w) = p₀(w)•D(e₀) + D(J(tail w)) = p₀(w)•(G(x) − F(x)) + A(tail w), so ‖D(w)‖ ≤ |p₀(w)|·‖G(x) − F(x)‖ + ‖A‖·‖tail w‖ ≤ (‖G(x) − F(x)‖ + ‖A‖)·‖w‖. The constant is ≥ 0, so ContinuousLinearMap.opNorm_le_bound gives ‖D‖ ≤ ‖G(x) − F(x)‖ + ‖A‖.
proof_key_steps: coordinates p₀, tail, J with ι(s,z) = s•e₀ + Jz, w = p₀(w)e₀ + J(tail w), |p₀ w|, ‖tail w‖ ≤ ‖w‖
H(y) := F(tail y) + p₀(y)•(G − F)(tail y) is C^∞ and affine in t along ι

chain rule along z ↦ ι(t,z) gives DH∘J = DF(x) + t(DG(x) − DF(x))

0. (LOC) denotes the locality conclusion of the sibling toolkit (dimred_mbl_dt_lpo_current_toolkit), available from (VO) and (REP). S(X) is compact: it is the image of the compact set Icc 0 1 ×ˢ spt X under the continuous map (t,x) ↦ ι(t,x) (WithLp.toLp, Fin.cons, WithLp.ofLp are continuous).
1. Slices of H. F, G, H are C^∞, hence differentiable. By the sibling affine_homotopy (ii) at t = 0 and t = 1, for all x, v: H(ι(0,x)) = F(x) + 0•(G x − F x) = F(x) and DH(ι(0,x))(Jv) = DF(x)v + 0•(…) = DF(x)v; H(ι(1,x)) = F(x) + 1•(G x − F x) = G(x) and DH(ι(1,x))(Jv) = DF(x)v + 1•(DG(x)v − DF(x)v) = DG(x)v.
2. Degree 0.
2.1. Apply the sibling cutoff (dimensions N+1 → N', degree 0, the C^∞ map H, the form ω, K = S(X)): there are θ'' ∈ 𝒟^0(ℝ^{N+1}) and an open W'' ⊇ S(X) with θ''(y) = H^#ω(y) and dθ''(y) = (dω(H y)).compContinuousLinearMap (DH y) for y ∈ W''.
2.2. By hypothesis θ = H^#(dω) on an open W_θ ⊇ S(X). Hence θ and the test form dθ'' = exteriorDerivativeTestOn univ 0 θ'' agree on the open set W_θ ∩ W'', which contains S(X) ⊇ spt C. By (LOC), C(θ) = C(dθ'') = ∂C(θ'') (GeometricCurrentOn.boundary_apply).
2.3. The boundary hypothesis for β := θ'' gives η₀, η₁ with η_s(x)(v) = θ''(ι(s,x))(J∘v) and ∂C(θ'') = X(η₁) − X(η₀).
2.4. X(η₀) = X(ηF): let W_F be the open set containing spt X on which ηF = F^#ω and V₀ := W_F ∩ {x : ι(0,x) ∈ W''}. V₀ is open (x ↦ ι(0,x) is continuous) and contains spt X (for x ∈ spt X, ι(0,x) ∈ S(X) ⊆ W'' since 0 ∈ [0,1]). For x ∈ V₀ and all v, by step 1 and ContinuousAlternatingMap.compContinuousLinearMap_apply: η₀(x)(v) = θ''(ι(0,x))(J∘v) = ω(H(ι(0,x)))(i ↦ DH(ι(0,x))(J v_i)) = ω(F x)(i ↦ DF(x)v_i) = (F^#ω)(x)(v) = ηF(x)(v). So η₀ = ηF on V₀ and (LOC) gives X(η₀) = X(ηF).
2.5. In the same way, with s = 1, G, the open set W_G on which ηG = G^#ω and V₁ := W_G ∩ {x : ι(1,x) ∈ W''}, we get η₁ = ηG on V₁ ⊇ spt X and X(η₁) = X(ηG).
2.6. Hence X(ηG) − X(ηF) = X(η₁) − X(η₀) = ∂C(θ'') = C(θ).
3. Degree k+1.
3.1. As in 2.1 with degree k+1: θ'' ∈ 𝒟^{k+1}(ℝ^{N+1}) and an open W'' ⊇ S(X) with θ'' = H^#ω and dθ'' = H^#(dω) on W''.
3.2. As in 2.2, θ = H^#(dω) = dθ'' on W_θ ∩ W'' ⊇ S(X) ⊇ spt C, so C(θ) = C(dθ'') = ∂C(θ'') by (LOC).
3.3. θ'' = H^#ω = θ' on the open set W'' ∩ W_θ' ⊇ S(X) ⊇ spt C', so C'(θ'') = C'(θ') by (LOC).
3.4. The boundary hypothesis for β := θ'' gives η₀, η₁ with η_s(x)(v) = θ''(ι(s,x))(J∘v) and ∂C(θ'') = X(η₁) − X(η₀) − C'(θ''); exactly as in 2.4–2.5 (now with v ∈ (ℝ^N)^{k+1}) X(η₀) = X(ηF) and X(η₁) = X(ηG).
3.5. Hence C(θ) = X(ηG) − X(ηF) − C'(θ'), i.e. X(ηG) − X(ηF) = C(θ) + C'(θ').

2.1. The sibling cutoff (N+1 → N', degree 0+1, H, the test form dω = exteriorDerivativeTestOn univ 0 ω, K = S) gives θ ∈ 𝒟^{0+1}(ℝ^{N+1}) and an open W ⊇ S with θ = H^#(dω) on W.
2.2. The sibling smooth_identity (degree 0) with C := cyl(X) (support in S by (C1); boundary relation = (C4) for X, which needs only compact support and finite mass), ω, ηF, ηG and θ gives X(ηG) − X(ηF) = cyl(X)(θ).
2.3. The sibling smooth_mass with k = 0, F, G, H, X, C := cyl(X) (relation = (C3) for X ∈ NC_0), β := dω (|dω| ≤ b), θ (θ(ι(t,x)) = H^#(dω)(ι(t,x)) for t ∈ [0,1], x ∈ spt X because ι(t,x) ∈ S ⊆ W) and Λ, δ gives |cyl(X)(θ)| ≤ δ·Λ^0·b·M(X).toReal.
2.4. For k = 0, boundaryMassOn X univ = 0, so the claimed right-hand side equals δ·(Λ^0·M(X).toReal·b + Λ^{0−1}·0·a) = δ·Λ^0·b·M(X).toReal, and 2.2–2.3 prove the claim.
3. Case k = k'+1.
3.1. boundaryMassOn X univ = M(∂X) < ∞. By the toolkit (NCB), spt ∂X ⊆ spt X, spt ∂X is compact and boundaryMassOn ∂X univ < ∞, so ∂X ∈ NC_{k'}. By (C1) for ∂X, spt cyl(∂X) ⊆ S(∂X) ⊆ S.
3.2. cutoff gives θ ∈ 𝒟^{k'+1+1}(ℝ^{N+1}) with θ = H^#(dω) on an open W ⊇ S, and θ' ∈ 𝒟^{k'+1}(ℝ^{N+1}) with θ' = H^#ω on an open W' ⊇ S.
3.3. smooth_identity (degree k'+1) with C := cyl(X), C' := cyl(∂X) (supports in S by 1 and 3.1; boundary relation = (C5) for X), ω, ηF, ηG, θ, θ' gives X(ηG) − X(ηF) = cyl(X)(θ) + cyl(∂X)(θ').

For i, j apply the sibling cauchy_estimate with the C^∞ maps F_i, F_j (derivative bound Λ on spt X), δ_{ij} := Λ/(i+1) + Λ/(j+1) (dist(F_i x, F_j x) ≤ dist(F_i x, F x) + dist(F x, F_j x) ≤ δ_{ij}), a_ω, b_ω, ηF := η°_i(ω), ηG := η°_j(ω): |X(η°_j(ω)) − X(η°_i(ω))| ≤ δ_{ij}·K_ω(Λ). Since δ_{ij} → 0 as i, j → ∞, (X(η°_j(ω)))_j is Cauchy in ℝ; let L(ω) be its limit (CauchySeq.tendsto_limUnder).
A4. (★) for L. Let Λ', Fs, ω, ηs be as in (★) and Λ'' := max(Λ, Λ'). Given ε > 0, uniform convergence gives j₀ with dist(F x, Fs_j x) < ε for j ≥ j₀, x ∈ spt X. For j ≥ j₀ apply cauchy_estimate with F' := F_j, G' := Fs_j (‖DF_j(x)‖ ≤ Λ ≤ Λ'' and ‖DFs_j(x)‖ ≤ Λ' ≤ Λ'' on spt X), δ := Λ/(j+1) + ε (dist(F_j x, Fs_j x) ≤ Λ/(j+1) + ε on spt X), a_ω, b_ω, ηF := η°_j(ω), ηG := ηs_j: |X(ηs_j) − X(η°_j(ω))| ≤ (Λ/(j+1) + ε)·K_ω(Λ''). A5. Linearity. For ω, ω' and r ∈ ℝ, the test forms η°_j(ω) + η°_j(ω') and r•η°_j(ω) equal F_j^#(ω + ω') on W_j(ω) ∩ W_j(ω') ⊇ spt X, resp. F_j^#(rω) on W_j(ω) ⊇ spt X, because α ↦ α.compContinuousLinearMap A is linear. A4 applied to the sequence (F_j) itself (C^∞, ‖DF_j‖ ≤ Λ, F_j → F uniformly) gives X(η°_j(ω) + η°_j(ω')) → L(ω + ω') and X(r•η°_j(ω)) → L(rω); by linearity of X these sequences equal X(η°_j(ω)) + X(η°_j(ω')) → L(ω) + L(ω') and r X(η°_j(ω)) → r L(ω). Given the data of CHAR (F Λ-Lipschitz, X NC, Fs, ω, ηs with the stated properties), the first case applies, so lpush N N' k F X is the current of Part A, and (★) — whose content does not involve the Lipschitz constant — gives X(ηs_j) → lpush N N' k F X (ω). subproblems.natural_proof:
0. Tools: (A0), (MB), (LOC), (NCD), (NCB) from the sibling toolkit; the support criterion (a) and closedness (b) of the reused support_calculus. Standard approximants: for Λ-Lipschitz F the sibling mollify gives C^∞ Λ-Lipschitz F_j with dist(F_j x, F x) ≤ Λ/(j+1), so F_j → F uniformly on ℝ^N (TendstoUniformly, hence TendstoUniformlyOn every set) and ‖DF_j(x)‖ ≤ Λ (norm_fderiv_le_of_lipschitz); for a compact K and a form ω the sibling cutoff gives test forms η_j and open W_j ⊇ K with η_j = F_j^#ω and dη_j = F_j^#(dω) on W_j.
1. (1) Let X ∈ NC_k(ℝ^N) and ω ∈ 𝒟^k(ℝ^N). Apply CHAR with Λ = 1, F = id (LipschitzWith 1 id), Fs_j := id (C^∞, ‖fderiv ℝ id x‖ = ‖ContinuousLinearMap.id‖ ≤ 1 =: Λ', a constant sequence equal to its limit converges uniformly) and ηs_j := ω (on W = univ, ω(x) = (ω(id x)).compContinuousLinearMap (ContinuousLinearMap.id) = ω(x)). The constant sequence X(ω) therefore converges to lpush N N k id X (ω), so lpush id X (ω) = X(ω) (tendsto_nhds_unique); GeometricCurrentOn.ext gives (1).
2. (2) Let F be Λ-Lipschitz and X, Y ∈ NC_k. By (NCD), X − Y ∈ NC_k and spt(X − Y) ⊆ spt X ∪ spt Y. Fix ω and take standard approximants with K := spt X ∪ spt Y. CHAR for X, Y and X − Y (all supports lie in W_j) gives X(η_j) → lpush F X ω, Y(η_j) → lpush F Y ω and (X − Y)(η_j) = X(η_j) − Y(η_j) → lpush F (X − Y) ω. Uniqueness of limits gives lpush F (X − Y) ω = lpush F X ω − lpush F Y ω = (lpush F X − lpush F Y)(ω); ext.
3. (3) Let F, G be Λ-Lipschitz with F = G on spt X. Take standard approximants (K = spt X). F_j → F uniformly on spt X, and since G = F there also F_j → G uniformly on spt X. CHAR for (F, F_j, η_j) and for (G, F_j, η_j) gives X(η_j) → lpush F X ω and X(η_j) → lpush G X ω; uniqueness of limits and ext give (3).
4. (4) Let F be Λ-Lipschitz and X ∈ NC_k.
4.1. Mass. Let ω and c satisfy |ω(y)| ≤ c for all y; take standard approximants (K = spt X). For x ∈ spt X ⊆ W_j, (L1) gives |η_j(x)| = |(ω(F_j x)).compContinuousLinearMap (DF_j x)| ≤ ‖DF_j(x)‖^k|ω(F_j x)| ≤ Λ^k c. By (A0), |X(η_j)| ≤ Λ^k c M(X).toReal; by CHAR and passage to the limit, |lpush F X ω| ≤ (Λ^k M(X).toReal)·c. By (MB), M(lpush F X) ≤ ofReal(Λ^k M(X).toReal) = (Λ : ℝ≥0∞)^k·M(X) (ENNReal.ofReal_mul, ENNReal.ofReal_pow, ENNReal.ofReal_coe_nnreal, ENNReal.ofReal_toReal since M(X) ≠ ∞).
4.2. Support. E := F '' spt X is compact, hence closed. By support_calculus (a) it suffices to show lpush F X ω = 0 whenever tsupport ω is disjoint from E. Then (tsupport ω)ᶜ is an open set containing the compact E, so IsCompact.exists_thickening_subset_open gives r > 0 with thickening r E ⊆ (tsupport ω)ᶜ. Choose j₀ with Λ/(j+1) < r for j ≥ j₀. For j ≥ j₀ and x ∈ spt X, dist(F_j x, F x) < r, so F_j(x) ∈ thickening r E and F_j(x) ∉ tsupport ω. Let V_j := W_j ∩ F_j⁻¹((tsupport ω)ᶜ), open and containing spt X. For x ∈ V_j, ω(F_j x) = 0 (image_eq_zero_of_notMem_tsupport), so η_j(x) = 0. By (LOC) with η' = 0, X(η_j) = X(0) = 0 for j ≥ j₀, and CHAR gives lpush F X ω = lim X(η_j) = 0. Hence spt(lpush F X) ⊆ F '' spt X.
5. (5) Let F be Λ-Lipschitz and X ∈ 𝒟_{k+1} with compact support, M(X) < ∞, M(∂X) < ∞; then X ∈ NC_{k+1} (boundaryMassOn X univ = M(∂X)) and, by (NCB), ∂X ∈ NC_k with spt ∂X ⊆ spt X. Fix ω ∈ 𝒟^k(ℝ^{N'}) and take standard approximants η_j (K = spt X) with η_j = F_j^#ω and dη_j = F_j^#(dω) on W_j. CHAR for X, the form dω and the test forms dη_j = exteriorDerivativeTestOn univ k η_j gives X(dη_j) → lpush F X (dω) = ∂(lpush F X)(ω) (boundary_apply). CHAR for ∂X, ω and η_j (W_j ⊇ spt X ⊇ spt ∂X) gives ∂X(η_j) → lpush F (∂X) ω. As ∂X(η_j) = X(dη_j), uniqueness of limits gives ∂(lpush F X)(ω) = lpush F (∂X)(ω); ext.
6. (6) Let F be Λ-Lipschitz and X ∈ NC_k. Take Fs := (F_j) from mollify: C^∞, Λ-Lipschitz, TendstoUniformly F_j F (dist ≤ Λ/(j+1) → 0 uniformly). Given ω, let η_j be standard approximants for K = spt X; η_j = F_j^#ω on the open W_j ⊇ spt X, and CHAR gives X(η_j) → lpush F X ω.

subproblems.natural_proof:
0. Common setup. Let F, G be Λ-Lipschitz, H L-Lipschitz and X a current of the relevant degree with compact support and finite mass such that H(ι(t,x)) = F(x) + t•(G(x) − F(x)) for x ∈ spt X, t ∈ [0,1]. S := S(X) is compact (continuous image of Icc 0 1 ×ˢ spt X). The sibling mollify gives C^∞ Λ-Lipschitz F_j, G_j with dist(F_j x, F x), dist(G_j x, G x) ≤ Λ/(j+1) and ‖DF_j‖, ‖DG_j‖ ≤ Λ; the sibling affine_homotopy (i) gives C^∞ H_j with H_j(ι(t,x)) = F_j(x) + t•(G_j(x) − F_j(x)) for all t, x. Since spt X is compact and G − F is continuous, there is D₀ ≥ 0 with ‖G(x) − F(x)‖ ≤ D₀ for x ∈ spt X (IsCompact.exists_bound_of_continuousOn).
0.1. Uniform convergence on S: for y = ι(t,x) ∈ S, H_j(y) − H(y) = (1 − t)(F_j x − F x) + t(G_j x − G x), so ‖H_j(y) − H(y)‖ ≤ (1 − t)Λ/(j+1) + tΛ/(j+1) = Λ/(j+1) → 0; hence H_j → H uniformly on S and on every subset.
0.2. Derivative bound on S: for y = ι(t,x) ∈ S, the norm part of affine_homotopy (ii) gives ‖DH_j(y)‖ ≤ ‖G_j x − F_j x‖ + ‖DF_j(x) + t•(DG_j(x) − DF_j(x))‖ ≤ (Λ/(j+1) + D₀ + Λ/(j+1)) + ((1 − t)Λ + tΛ) ≤ Λ' := D₀ + 3Λ.
0.3. For a test form β on ℝ^{N'} the sibling cutoff (H_j, β, K = S) gives θ_j(β) with θ_j(β) = H_j^#β on an open W_j ⊇ S. Consequently, for every NC current Y on ℝ^{N+1} with spt Y ⊆ S, CHAR (H L-Lipschitz, Fs := H_j, Λ' from 0.2, uniform convergence on spt Y from 0.1, ηs_j := θ_j(β)) gives Y(θ_j(β)) → lpush H Y β.
0.4. With ηF_j, ηG_j := cutoff pull-backs of ω by F_j, G_j near spt X, CHAR for F (Fs := F_j, Λ' := Λ) and for G gives X(ηF_j) → lpush F X ω and X(ηG_j) → lpush G X ω.
1. (10) Degree 0: X ∈ NC_0 (boundaryMassOn = 0 in degree 0). By (C1), cyl(X) ∈ NC_{0+1}(ℝ^{N+1}) (compact support, mass ≤ M(X) < ∞, boundary mass < ∞) with spt cyl(X) ⊆ S. Fix ω ∈ 𝒟^0(ℝ^{N'}). The sibling smooth_identity (degree 0) for F_j, G_j, H_j, C := cyl(X) (relation (C4)), ω, ηF_j, ηG_j and θ_j := θ_j(dω) gives X(ηG_j) − X(ηF_j) = cyl(X)(θ_j). By 0.4 the left side tends to lpush G X ω − lpush F X ω; by 0.3 the right side tends to lpush H (cyl X)(dω) = ∂(lpush H (cyl X))(ω). Uniqueness of limits and ext give (10).
2. (11) Degree k+1: X ∈ NC_{k+1} (boundaryMassOn X univ = M(∂X)); by the toolkit (NCB), ∂X ∈ NC_k with spt ∂X ⊆ spt X; by (C1), cyl(X) and cyl(∂X) are NC with supports in S(X) and S(∂X) ⊆ S. Fix ω ∈ 𝒟^{k+1}(ℝ^{N'}). smooth_identity (degree k+1) with C := cyl(X), C' := cyl(∂X) (relation (C5)), θ_j := θ_j(dω), θ'_j := θ_j(ω) gives X(ηG_j) − X(ηF_j) = cyl(X)(θ_j) + cyl(∂X)(θ'_j). Passing to the limit (0.4, and 0.3 for Y = cyl X and Y = cyl ∂X): lpush G X ω − lpush F X ω = ∂(lpush H (cyl X))(ω) + lpush H (cyl ∂X)(ω). Rearranging and ext give (11).
3. (12) Degree k: X ∈ NC_k and dist(F x, G x) ≤ δ on spt X. Put δ⁺ := max(δ, 0). Fix ω ∈ 𝒟^{k+1}(ℝ^{N'}) and c with |ω(y)| ≤ c for all y. For x ∈ spt X, dist(F_j x, G_j x) ≤ Λ/(j+1) + δ + Λ/(j+1) ≤ δ_j := δ⁺ + 2Λ/(j+1). smooth_mass with F_j, G_j, H_j, X, C := cyl(X) (relation (C3)), Λ, δ_j, b := c, β := ω and θ := θ_j(ω) (θ_j(ω)(ι(t,x)) = H_j^#ω(ι(t,x)) for t ∈ [0,1], x ∈ spt X, as ι(t,x) ∈ S ⊆ W_j) gives |cyl(X)(θ_j(ω))| ≤ δ_j Λ^k c M(X).toReal. By 0.3 (Y = cyl X) cyl(X)(θ_j(ω)) → lpush H (cyl X) ω, hence |lpush H (cyl X) ω| ≤ (δ⁺ Λ^k M(X).toReal)·c. The toolkit (MB) gives M(lpush H (cyl X)) ≤ ofReal(δ⁺ Λ^k M(X).toReal) = ofReal δ⁺ · (Λ:ℝ≥0∞)^k · M(X) = ofReal δ · Λ^k · M(X) ≤ ofReal δ · (2Λ)^k · M(X) (ENNReal.ofReal_mul with δ⁺ ≥ 0, ENNReal.ofReal_pow, ENNReal.ofReal_coe_nnreal, ENNReal.ofReal_toReal as M(X) < ∞, ofReal (max δ 0) = ofReal δ, and Λ^k ≤ (2Λ)^k in ℝ≥0∞ by pow_le_pow_left).
